transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Sahil (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Aisha, Marco, Lena, Omar (Bluefin)

Auto-summary (auto): Weekly POC sync; focused on routing / canary / cutover and telemetry signals.

Topics: heatmap-driven routing; canary signals and gating; runbook handover; security checklist; next steps

[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, we have a packed agenda but mainly to go over the heatmap that Sahil put together and nail down canary cues and the cutover playbook, and then handoff the runbook.
[00:22] Aisha: yep good morning, excited to see the heatmap, Marco's been running the prod-ish traces this week so we can align on real traffic.
[00:35] Sahil: cool, I pushed a first pass to the shared folder, it's per-model and per-endpoint, shows median/95/99 and also a column for KV cache hit-rate, that last part is noisy cause of the sampling but you can see the hotspots.
[01:07] Marco: um hmm, on that cache column I think the sample got aggregated, so the numbers look higher than they actually are at tail, but pattern is right, you can see longer tails on the long-context prompts.
[01:45] Jamie: right, so for routing recommendations we have two levers: route by latency heatzones (keep latency SLO) or route by cost (fallback to smaller quantized models) and of course we can mix via traffic weights.
[02:10] Lena: quick security note, anything that moves off private deployment we need to log, and we need KMS usage details, SOC2 controls, like audit logs. we'll pass the checklist later.
[02:40] Sahil: copying that, in the heatmap we flagged any endpoint with p99 > 1.2s as red, between .6 and 1.2 amber, below .6 green — those thresholds came from your previous SLO doc but we can update.
[03:12] Omar: is that end-to-end or just inference time? our tracing shows additional network jitter sometimes.
[03:25] Marco: good point, heatmap is inference-only; we added a note to show estimated e2e by adding avg network tail. Sahil, do you have that overlay?
[03:38] Sahil: yeah overlay exists but it's rough, we can refine with Marco's traces.
[04:05] Jamie: ok on canary signals — the group agreed last week to monitor: request rate, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and qualitative quality regression on a prompt set. We propose automatic rollback when p99 increases by >25% or error-rate >1% sustained for 5m. Thoughts?
[04:45] Marco: 25% p99 seems aggressive given spikes; can we gate on absolute thresholds plus relative change? e.g., p99 >1.4s or +30%?
[05:05] Sahil: yes combining absolute and relative is safer — we'll document two-tier gates. Also suggest a short quiet-window for signal stabilization — 10 minutes after ramp to measure steady-state.
[05:30] Aisha: we want to avoid noisy early rollbacks, we prefer manual hold for first dry-run then auto for subsequent runs.
[05:45] Jamie: noted — plan: first canary dry-run will be manual abort only, then switch to auto rollback for the production cutover.
[06:01] Priya: we'll capture that in the runbook.
[06:15] [TRANSCRIPT GLITCH - timestamp drift]
[06:30] Marco: on routing matrix, thought was to route 5% to new variant, 20% to quantized fallback, remainder to primary. but we can start with 1% for initial sanity.
[07:00] Sahil: heatmap suggests certain prompt types spike — we can set per-route weights: for high-context prompts route to bigger model; for short prompts route to trimmed model. This needs application-level tagging though.
[07:28] Aisha: tagging is doable but will need a small change to our front-end to mark context length, we can do that in a sprint.
[07:41] Omar: who owns the traffic shift orchestrations during cutover? we need a single source of truth for routing decisions.
[07:55] Jamie: Redwood can host the routing matrix config in the console, and we'll give you a git-backed JSON so you can review changes — but Bluefin will own the final flip.
[08:15] Lena: on audit logs, need retention window details, and whether logs include full request bodies or just metadata. that's must for compliance.
[08:30] Jamie: default is metadata only for logs in hosted; request bodies can be redacted unless customer opts-in for deeper debugging; we'll include that in the security appendix.
[09:00] Marco: about the KV cache note — when the cache warms, latency drops substantially for repeated prefixes, can we make the canary warm that cache?
[09:20] Sahil: yes we have a warm-up step in the runbook — pre-seed frequent prefixes for the canary so it's not penalized. but that changes the signal, so we capture both cold and warm metrics.
[09:50] Aisha: good, please show both in the heatmap export.
[10:10] Sahil: will do.
[10:30] [15:00] Jamie: (fast-forwarded) Runbook discussion: cutover phases we propose: preflight checks (30m), staged ramp (1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 100% over configurable windows), quiet-windows at each ramp step to evaluate signals, and a rollback plan mapped to the fallback model variants and traffic gates.
[15:35] Marco: can we add a blue-green option? some of our infra prefers blue-green with DNS-based switch.
[15:50] Jamie: blue-green is supported but heavier — need double capacity during the hold. We'll document cost impact.
[16:12] Aisha: cost matters — show expected token cost delta for each rollout strategy in the runbook.
[16:30] Sahil: noted, we'll add cost delta estimates per step.
[16:45] Lena: also escalate paths — who to call at 2am if rollback fails? need phone numbers plus escalation matrix.
[17:00] Priya: we'll include a contact table; Redwood oncall and Bluefin oncall.
[17:20] [20:00] Marco: telemetry question: what dashboards will you hand over? we need latency heatmap, per-route p95/p99, error waterfall, and a quality regression panel showing prompt set diffs.
[20:35] Sahil: yes those four are standard; we'll also include token breakdown per route.
[20:50] Aisha: for the quality regression panel, will you show the exact model outputs or summaries? showing outputs raises PII concerns.
[21:05] Jamie: we can show diffs and hashes for matching plus anonymized snippets; full outputs only with explicit permission and redaction.
[21:30] Omar: can we run an A/B for 48 hours on 5% traffic to collect quality metrics before big ramp?
[21:45] Marco: yes that fits our internal approval process.
[22:00] Sahil: we'll instrument the A/B and collect side-by-side metrics; recommended min sample size computed in the doc.
[22:12] [25:00] Jamie: timeline recap: heatmap refinement by next Friday, canary dry-run week of 4/6, runbook delivered tomorrow-ish, security checklist by 4/6, full cutover target 4/13 pending results.
[25:30] Aisha: okay good.
[25:45] Marco: quick nit on metric names — please standardize metric tag names with our telemetry so Grafana maps automatically.
[26:00] Sahil: we'll share tag mapping CSV.
[26:25] Lena: re: encryption, if we go with private deployment some items change; can we get a matrix that lists differences between hosted/dedicated/private?
[26:40] Jamie: yes, Redwood will produce a concise matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and call out KMS, audit log, and network topology differences.
[27:05] Omar: who is doing the smoke test plan?
[27:15] Priya: Redwood will own smoke scripts, Bluefin will schedule execution during quiet-window.
[27:40] Marco: please include expected failure modes and mitigation steps — e.g., sudden memory pressure on GPU, spike in bad prompts, KV cache thrash.
[28:05] Sahil: will document mitigation and a circuit-breaker parameter table.
[28:30] [30:00] Jamie: ok we're nearing the end — any blockers?
[30:10] Aisha: none besides final confirmation of SLO numbers and the security checklist.
[30:25] Lena: we'll need the checklist by 4/6 to sign off for the pilot.
[30:40] Jamie: understood.
[31:00] Marco: one more ask — can Redwood run a short load test to validate ramp plan? 20-minute ramp to 50% traffic to capture autoscaling and tail behaviour.
[31:20] Sahil: yes we can coordinate a load test during the dry-run and share logs; will need a window.
[31:35] Omar: prefer early morning slot, we'll coordinate.
[31:50] Jamie: action items recap, owner-led, due dates as recorded.
[32:10] [40:00] (wrap-up) Jamie: thanks everyone, we'll update the heatmap, send the runbook and matrix, and reconvene after the heatmap refinement. Next sync scheduled for 2026-04-06 but we'll send a calendar hold.
[40:30] Aisha: thanks all.
[40:45] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-heard words, speaker boundaries approximate. Some timestamps approximate due to recording artifacts.
